_note: SAMPLED, NOT EXHAUSTIVE. gitea is ~6,200 files and this audit read the loop-bearing data-access paths in models/, services/ and routers/ rather than every file. Precision scored against it is therefore a FLOOR, not a precision figure — see bench/score.mjs. Recall @ high is meaningful: each entry below was confirmed by reading the whole enclosing function. Migrations under modelmigration/ were excluded by rule (they run once at install), and gitea has many query-in-loop sites there.
_auditedBy: Claude, blind to speeDB output for this repository
queriesNow: 1 IsOrganizationMember per collaborator, plus up to 2 DELETEs per collaborator
queriesAfter: 1 membership query for all collaborator ids, and one DELETE with an IN list
why: `for _, c := range collaborators` calls organization.IsOrganizationMember(ctx, newOwner.ID, c.ID) once per collaborator, and issues sess.Delete per collaborator alongside it; both are set operations written one row at a time.
_lineNote: EDITED AFTER SEEING RESULTS — judge this, do not take it on trust. Originally recorded as the single line 196, the IsOrganizationMember call. That was inconsistent with this entry's own `why`, which already described the per-collaborator sess.Delete calls at 191 and 206 as part of the same defect: one loop doing per-iteration database work three ways. Recording a multi-line defect as one line was an error in the audit, not a concession to the tool. `lines` is the established mechanism for this — mt-test-studio's truth file uses it for admin_views.py:1030/1048/1081 with the note 'A finding at any of these lines is that defect.' This changes candidate coverage (191 and 206 are candidates) but NOT recall: the scored run published no finding anywhere in transfer.go, so recall @ high stays 0% either way.

queriesNow: 1 UPDATE per already-known language and 1 INSERT per new language, inside a loop nested in a scan of oldstats
queriesAfter: one bulk INSERT and one bulk UPDATE for the whole language set
why: `for lang, size := range stats` writes each language individually; XORM accepts a slice for Insert, and the update set is known before the loop begins.

queriesNow: 1 INSERT per schedule row, then 1 INSERT per spec of that row
queriesAfter: 1 bulk INSERT for the rows, 1 bulk INSERT for all specs
why: Nested `for _, row := range rows` / `for _, spec := range row.Specs` insert one row at a time inside a single transaction; the whole set is in memory before the loop starts.

queriesNow: 1 UPDATE per existing license, 1 INSERT per new one
why: Same shape as UpdateLanguageStats. Rated lower because a repository has one or two licences, so the row count is small in practice.
